question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My mother said / that the thief / Ramesh will learnt / his lesson soon.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Ramesh will learnt.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• After the modal verb "will", the base form (V1) of the verb must be used, never the past form (V2). "learnt" is the past/participle form of "learn", so "will learnt" is grammatically wrong; it should be "will learn".

◦ Correct: My mother said that the thief Ramesh will learn his lesson soon.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "My mother said", "that the thief" and "his lesson soon" contain no error.

• Verb forms of learn: learn (V1) – learnt/learned (V2) – learnt/learned (V3).

NOTE

• Modal verbs (will, shall, can, could, may, might, must, should, would) are always followed by the bare infinitive (V1): will go, can do, must learn — never "will went" or "will learnt".

question:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word in the given sentence.

James is just an old eccentric.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Cranky.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Eccentric" means strange, unconventional or odd in behaviour. Its closest synonym is "cranky", which also means odd, strange or peculiar. (सनकी / विचित्र)

◦ Example: The eccentric/cranky old man kept dozens of clocks in his room.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "Ordinary" (normal, usual) is nearly an antonym of eccentric.

• Option 2 "Follower" (a supporter) and Option 4 "Humble" (modest) are unrelated in meaning.

NOTE

• Synonyms of eccentric: cranky, quirky, odd, peculiar, unconventional, whimsical. Antonyms: ordinary, normal, conventional. "Eccentric" can be an adjective (eccentric habits) or a noun (an old eccentric = an odd person).

question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

After the match, / the stadium was the messiest / it's ever been.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. No Error.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The sentence is grammatically correct as it stands: "After the match, the stadium was the messiest it's ever been."

◦ "the messiest" is the correct superlative of "messy" (messy – messier – messiest), and the structure "the + superlative + (that) it has ever been" is a standard English pattern.

◦ "it's ever been" = "it has ever been" — the present perfect with "ever" correctly conveys "at any time until now".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "After the match" is a correct prepositional phrase of time.

• Compare similar correct patterns: "This is the best film I have ever seen"; "She is the happiest she has ever been."

NOTE

• Superlative + present perfect + "ever" is a very common SSC pattern: "the + superlative + subject + have/has ever + V3". Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y form the superlative with "-iest" (messy → messiest, happy → happiest).

question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

According to the chairman, his proposal was ___________ than Mr. Jackson's.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. worse.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word "than" in the sentence demands the comparative degree. The comparative of "bad" is "worse" (bad – worse – worst).

◦ Correct: ... his proposal was worse than Mr. Jackson's.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "worst" is the superlative (used with "the", not with "than").

• Option 3 "bad" is the positive degree and cannot be followed by "than".

• Option 4 "ill" means unwell and does not fit a proposal.

NOTE

• Irregular degrees of comparison: bad/ill – worse – worst; good/well – better – best; little – less – least; much/many – more – most. With "than" always use the comparative form.

question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an error in phrasal verb.

Gita got onto / the book / she was reading / this morning.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Gita got onto.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb "got onto" is wrongly used here. "Get onto" means to make contact with someone or to move on to a new topic — it cannot mean continuing with a book.

• The correct phrasal verb is "got on with", which means continued doing something. (जारी रखना)

◦ Correct: Gita got on with the book she was reading this morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "the book", "she was reading" and "this morning" contain no error.

• Phrasal verbs with "get": get on with (continue; have a good relationship), get onto (contact; move to a topic), get over (recover from), get away with (escape punishment), get by (manage).

NOTE

• SSC frequently tests "get" phrasal verbs — remember: get up (rise), get along (be friendly), get through (pass/complete), get off (alight), get at (imply/reach).

question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the highlighted group of words in the given sentence.

The tailor was called to stitch the long loose gowns worn by priests and choristers.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. cassocks.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A "cassock" is a long, loose gown (usually full-length) worn by priests, members of the clergy and choristers during religious services. (पादरियों का लंबा चोगा)

◦ Correct: The tailor was called to stitch the cassocks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "frocks" (dresses, usually for girls/women), Option 3 "petticoats" (undergarments worn beneath a skirt/saree) and Option 4 "tuxedos" (men's formal dinner suits) do not describe priests' gowns.

NOTE

• Related one-word substitutes/clerical dress: cassock (priest's gown), surplice (loose white vestment worn over the cassock), mitre (bishop's headdress), habit (a monk's/nun's dress).

question:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word from the given sentence.

The explorer's adventuros spirit led to the discovery of an ancient civilisation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. Adventuros.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Adventuros" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "adventurous", meaning willing to take risks; daring; fond of adventure. (साहसी)

◦ Correct: The explorer's adventurous spirit led to the discovery of an ancient civilisation.

• Spelling key: ADVENTURE + OUS = adventurous (note the "u" before the final "-ous").

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• "Ancient" (very old), "discovery" (the act of finding) and "explorer's" (belonging to an explorer) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Common "-ous" spellings tested in SSC: adventurous, courageous, mischievous (not "mischievious"), grievous (not "grievious"), humorous, courteous. Related forms: adventure (noun) → adventurous (adjective) → adventurously (adverb).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment without changing its meaning in the given sentence.

Entrepreneurial endeavours drive economic growth and innovation, empowering individuals to bring their ideas to fruition.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. ventures contribute to economic flourishing.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The underlined segment "endeavours drive economic growth" means entrepreneurial efforts promote/boost the economy. The only option that keeps this positive meaning is "ventures contribute to economic flourishing" — "ventures" = endeavours/undertakings, "contribute to ... flourishing" = drive growth.

◦ Correct: Entrepreneurial ventures contribute to economic flourishing and innovation ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "pursuits manipulates economic success" has a subject–verb agreement error (plural "pursuits" with singular "manipulates") and "manipulates" changes the meaning negatively.

• Option 3 "spur economic recession" and Option 4 "discourage economic prosperity" reverse the meaning — a recession is a decline, and "discourage" is the opposite of "drive".

NOTE

• Useful vocabulary: venture (a risky undertaking/business), fruition (the fulfilment of a plan — "bring ideas to fruition"), flourish (to thrive/prosper), recession (a period of economic decline).

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

I had to choose the best of the two options available.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. better of.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• When a comparison is between two persons or things, the comparative degree with "the" is used — "the better of the two", not "the best of the two". The superlative "best" is used only for three or more.

◦ Correct: I had to choose the better of the two options available.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "good of" (positive degree) does not express the comparison.

• Option 3 "better than" is wrong here because the structure is "the ... of the two", which needs "of", not "than".

• Option 4 "best than" is grammatically impossible — a superlative is never followed by "than".

NOTE

• Rule: "the + comparative + of the two" (the taller of the two boys) but "the + superlative + of the three/all" (the tallest of the three boys). This selection rule is a favourite in SSC error-spotting.

question:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.

I started feeling tired as I had been working for a long time and so I decided to call the day.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. call it a day.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "call it a day" means to stop working for the day; to decide that one has done enough. The pronoun "it" is essential — "call the day" is not an idiom. (दिन भर के काम को समाप्त करना)

◦ Correct: ... I had been working for a long time and so I decided to call it a day.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "be a day for calling" and Option 3 "be called a day" are meaningless constructions.

• Option 4 "call off the day" is wrong — "call off" means to cancel (e.g., call off a strike), not to stop working for the day.

NOTE

• Related idioms: "call it a night" (stop an evening activity), "down tools" (stop work), "wrap up" (finish). Distinguish "call it a day" (stop work) from "call off" (cancel) and "call on" (visit).

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

The farmer stood by the roadside stand to sell his _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. produce.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Produce" (as a noun, stressed on the first syllable) means agricultural products such as fruits, vegetables and grains. A farmer sells his produce at a roadside stand. (कृषि उपज)

◦ Correct: The farmer stood by the roadside stand to sell his produce.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "volume" (amount/a book), Option 2 "consequence" (result) and Option 3 "productivity" (the rate of production, an abstract quality) cannot be sold by a farmer.

NOTE

• Distinguish: produce (noun — farm products), product (a manufactured item), production (the process of producing), productivity (efficiency of production). "Produce" as a verb (pro-DUCE) means to make/create.

question:
Identify the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets.

Her candid remarks were a (refreshing) change from the usual diplomatic responses.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. Stale.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Refreshing" means pleasantly new, fresh and stimulating. Its antonym is "stale", meaning no longer fresh; dull and uninteresting because of overuse. (ताज़गी भरा का विलोम — बासी/नीरस)

◦ Example: His jokes had become stale, no longer a refreshing change.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Options 1 "Bracing" (fresh and invigorating), 2 "Invigorating" (energising) and 3 "Revitalising" (giving new life) are all synonyms of refreshing, not antonyms.

NOTE

• Synonyms of refreshing: bracing, invigorating, revitalising, rejuvenating. Antonyms: stale, tiring, boring, wearisome. Also note "candid" = frank/honest (स्पष्टवादी).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM for the underlined word in the given sentence.

He is a lazy person.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. hardworking.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lazy" means unwilling to work or use energy; idle. Its antonym is "hardworking", meaning diligent and industrious. (आलसी का विलोम — मेहनती)

◦ Example: Unlike his lazy brother, Ravi is extremely hardworking.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "perfect" (flawless), Option 3 "casual" (relaxed/informal) and Option 4 "popular" (liked by many) are not opposites of lazy.

NOTE

• Synonyms of lazy: idle, indolent, sluggish, lethargic, slothful. Antonyms: hardworking, diligent, industrious, energetic, active.

question:
In the following sentence the underlined part contains an error. Alternatives to the underlined part are given as options. Select the correct alternative.

Wolfia is the tiny plant in the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 2 i.e. tiniest.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase "in the world" indicates a comparison with all plants, which requires the superlative degree with "the" — "the tiniest plant in the world".

◦ Correct: Wolfia is the tiniest plant in the world.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 2.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "tinier" and Option 4 "more tiny" are comparatives — they need "than", which is absent.

• Option 3 "most tiny" is wrong because short adjectives ending in "-y" take "-iest", not "most" (tiny → tiniest, like happy → happiest).

NOTE

• "The + superlative + in/of ..." is the standard superlative frame: the tallest boy in the class, the tiniest plant in the world. (Fact: Wolffia, or duckweed, is indeed the world's smallest flowering plant.)

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. Abodomen.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Abodomen" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "abdomen", meaning the part of the body between the chest and the pelvis; the belly. (उदर / पेट)

◦ Example: The doctor examined the patient's abdomen.

• Spelling key: AB + DO + MEN — there is no "o" between "b" and "d".

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Abolished" (put an end to), "adverse" (unfavourable) and "annoyed" (irritated) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• Related forms: abdomen (noun) → abdominal (adjective — abdominal pain). Also distinguish adverse (unfavourable — adverse weather) from averse (unwilling — averse to risk), a frequent SSC confusable pair.

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

He is going to _________ the campaign against excessive use of _________ in local production units.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. lead.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Lead" means to head, direct or be in charge of something. "To lead a campaign" is the natural collocation — he is going to head/direct the campaign against excessive use (of harmful material) in local production units. (नेतृत्व करना)

◦ Correct: He is going to lead the campaign against excessive use ... in local production units.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "combat" (to fight against) would wrongly mean he is fighting the campaign itself, not leading it.

• Option 2 "spice" (to add flavour) is meaningless here.

• Option 3 "protest" is used as "protest against something"; "protest the campaign" would also reverse the intended sense.

NOTE

• Collocations with "campaign": lead/launch/run/spearhead a campaign. Verb forms: lead – led – led. Do not confuse the verb "lead" (to guide) with the metal "lead" (सीसा), which is spelt the same but pronounced "led".

question:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Please turn off the lights _________ leaving the house.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. before.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Before" indicates that one action happens earlier than another. Logically, the lights must be turned off before leaving the house. (पहले)

◦ Correct: Please turn off the lights before leaving the house.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "between" needs two points/objects (between 5 and 6 o'clock).

• Option 3 "during" and Option 4 "amid" mean "in the middle of" — you cannot switch off the lights while in the act of leaving in this context; the natural sequence is "before leaving".

NOTE

• "Before/after + V-ing" is a standard gerund construction: "before leaving", "after finishing". Prepositions of time: before (earlier), after (later), during (throughout a period), between (two limits).

question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. Disapoint.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Disapoint" is misspelt. The correct spelling is "disappoint" — with double "p" — meaning to fail to fulfil someone's hopes or expectations. (निराश करना)

◦ Example: I did not want to disappoint my parents.

• Spelling key: DIS + APPOINT = disappoint (one "s", two "p"s).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Consensus" (general agreement), "conceive" (to imagine/form an idea) and "disappear" (to vanish) are all correctly spelt.

NOTE

• "Conceive" follows the rule "i before e except after c" (receive, deceive, conceive). Related forms: disappoint → disappointment, disappointed, disappointing.

question:
Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Sree did not go to work today, as she was feeling a bit under the weather.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. feeling ill.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom "under the weather" means slightly ill or unwell. So "feeling a bit under the weather" = "feeling ill". (अस्वस्थ / तबीयत ठीक न होना)

◦ Correct: Sree did not go to work today, as she was feeling ill.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "feeling nervous" (anxious), Option 2 "feeling tired" (fatigued) and Option 3 "feeling excited" (thrilled) do not convey illness, which is the exact sense of the idiom.

NOTE

• Health-related idioms: "under the weather" (unwell), "as fit as a fiddle" (in perfect health), "back on one's feet" (recovered), "at death's door" (seriously ill).

question:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

The family members described their dream home's architectural elegance.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. coarseness.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Elegance" means grace, refinement and tasteful beauty. Its antonym is "coarseness", meaning roughness, crudeness or lack of refinement. (लालित्य का विलोम — भद्दापन/अशिष्टता)

◦ Example: The palace's elegance stood in contrast to the coarseness of the old barracks.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "fortitude" (courage in adversity) and Option 4 "gleam" (a shine/flash of light) are unrelated.

• Option 3 "grandiosity" (impressive showiness) is closer to a related idea of grandeur, not an opposite of elegance.

NOTE

• Synonyms of elegance: grace, refinement, sophistication, poise. Antonyms: coarseness, crudeness, vulgarity, inelegance.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the 'Age of Reason', is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the 'long' 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as 'decisive in the formation of modernity'. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the 'modern world'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 1..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. rigorous.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Rigorous" means thorough, exhaustive and strict. The Enlightenment is described as a period of "rigorous scientific, political, and philosophical debate" — i.e., intense and thorough intellectual debate. (कठोर / गहन)

◦ Correct: ... the period of rigorous scientific, political, and philosophical debate ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "auspicious" (favourable, promising success) and Option 2 "malicious" (intending harm) do not describe the nature of debate here.

• Option 3 "cautions" is a noun/verb form ("warnings"/"warns") and cannot act as an adjective before "scientific ... debate".

NOTE

• Synonyms of rigorous: thorough, meticulous, exacting, stringent. The Enlightenment ('Age of Reason') was the 17th–18th century European intellectual movement emphasising reason and science — thinkers included Voltaire, Rousseau, Locke and Kant.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the 'Age of Reason', is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the 'long' 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as 'decisive in the formation of modernity'. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the 'modern world'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 2..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 3 i.e. throughout.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Throughout" means during the whole period of. The debate characterised European culture "throughout the 'long' 18th century" — i.e., during that entire era (late 17th century to 1815). (पूरे समय / सम्पूर्ण अवधि में)

◦ Correct: ... characterised European culture throughout the 'long' 18th century ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 3.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "above" indicates position, not duration.

• Option 2 "over with" means "finished" (get it over with) and Option 4 "along with" means "together with" — neither expresses duration across a period.

NOTE

• "Throughout + period" = from the beginning to the end of that period (throughout the year, throughout history). The "long 18th century" is a historians' term for the period from the late 1600s to 1815 (end of the Napoleonic Wars).

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the 'Age of Reason', is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the 'long' 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as 'decisive in the formation of modernity'. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the 'modern world'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 3..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 4 i.e. shift.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Shift" (as a noun) means a change in position, direction or way of thinking. The Enlightenment was "an era of an enormous shift in thinking and reason" — a huge change in the way people thought. (बदलाव / परिवर्तन)

◦ Correct: This was an era of an enormous shift in thinking and reason ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

• Option 1 "secure" (to make safe) and Option 2 "shield" (to protect) suggest protection, not change.

• Option 3 "embed" (to fix firmly inside) is a verb and gives no sense of transformation in thought.

NOTE

• "Paradigm shift" is a common phrase for a fundamental change in approach. Synonyms of shift (noun): change, transformation, transition, swing. Historian Roy Porter called this shift 'decisive in the formation of modernity'.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the 'Age of Reason', is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the 'long' 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as 'decisive in the formation of modernity'. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the 'modern world'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. discarded.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Discarded" means thrown away, abandoned or given up. Centuries of custom and tradition were "discarded in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance ..." — old traditions were abandoned and replaced by new values. (त्याग दिया गया)

◦ Correct: Centuries of custom and tradition were discarded in favour of exploration ...

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "demean" (to lower someone's dignity) is a base verb — grammatically the blank needs a past participle after "were".

• Option 3 "dejected" (sad, downcast) describes a person's mood, not what happens to traditions.

• Option 4 "defrosted" (thawed from a frozen state) is absurd in this context.

NOTE

• "Discarded in favour of X" = given up so that X could be adopted. Synonyms of discard: abandon, reject, jettison, cast aside. Antonyms: retain, keep, preserve.

question:
In the following passage, some words have been deleted. Read the passage carefully and select the most appropriate option to fill in each blank.

The Enlightenment, sometimes known as the 'Age of Reason', is described as the period of (1)________ scientific, political, and philosophical debate that characterised European culture (2) ________ the 'long' 18th century: from the late 17th century until the end of the Napoleonic Wars in 1815. This was an era of an enormous (3) ________ in thinking and reason, which historian Roy Porter describes as 'decisive in the formation of modernity'. Centuries of custom and tradition were (4) ________ in favour of exploration, individuality, tolerance, and scientific (5) ________, all of which contributed to the formation of the 'modern world'.

Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 5..
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. endeavour.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Endeavour" (noun) means a serious, determined effort or attempt. "Scientific endeavour" — serious scientific effort — fits perfectly with the Enlightenment values of exploration, individuality and tolerance. (प्रयास)

◦ Correct: ... individuality, tolerance, and scientific endeavour, all of which contributed to the formation of the 'modern world'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 1.

Additional Information

• Option 2 "shirk" (to avoid work), Option 3 "slacken" (to slow down/loosen) and Option 4 "doodle" (to scribble absent-mindedly) all convey avoidance or idleness — the opposite of the passage's spirit of effort and progress.

NOTE

• "Endeavour" (British spelling) / "endeavor" (American). Synonyms: effort, attempt, enterprise, undertaking. The phrase "scientific endeavour" is a fixed collocation for organised scientific effort.

question: The Hindi novel 'Jhutha Sach' is written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Yashpal.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The famous Hindi novel "Jhutha Sach" (झूठा सच) was written by Yashpal. It is considered one of the greatest Hindi novels on the Partition of India (1947), published in two volumes — *Vatan aur Desh* (1958) and *Desh ka Bhavishya* (1960).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Yashpal was also a revolutionary associated with the Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA). His other works include *Divya*, *Dada Comrade* and *Meri Teri Uski Baat* (which won him the Sahitya Akademi Award, 1976).

• Jaishankar Prasad — famous for the epic *Kamayani*; Shrilal Shukla — *Raag Darbari* (Jnanpith awardee); Premchand — *Godaan*, *Gaban*, *Nirmala*.

NOTE

• SSC often asks author–book pairs from Hindi literature: *Kamayani* – Jaishankar Prasad, *Raag Darbari* – Shrilal Shukla, *Godaan* – Premchand, *Jhutha Sach* – Yashpal.

question: 'Attolu Eidu' is the cultural festival of which of the following union territories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lakshadweep.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Attolu Eidu" is a traditional cultural festival of the union territory of Lakshadweep. It is celebrated by the island communities with community feasts, folk songs and traditional performances. (लक्षद्वीप का सांस्कृतिक पर्व)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Lakshadweep is India's smallest union territory (by area and population), a group of 36 coral islands in the Arabian Sea; its capital is Kavaratti.

• Languages spoken are Malayalam and Mahl (in Minicoy). Popular folk dances include Lava dance (Minicoy), Kolkali and Parichakali.

NOTE

• Festivals of island territories: Lakshadweep — Eid festivals, Attolu Eidu, Lava dance performances; Andaman and Nicobar Islands — Island Tourism Festival.

question: According Census 2011 of India, which of the following union territories has the second highest literacy rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Daman and Diu.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the Census 2011, among the union territories, Lakshadweep had the highest literacy rate (91.85%) and "Daman and Diu" had the second highest literacy rate (87.10%). (दमन और दीव — 87.10%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Literacy rates of UTs (Census 2011): Lakshadweep 91.85%, Daman & Diu 87.10%, Andaman & Nicobar Islands 86.63%, Delhi 86.21%, Chandigarh 86.05%, Puducherry 85.85%, Dadra & Nagar Haveli 76.24%.

• India's overall literacy rate (2011) was 74.04% (males 82.14%, females 65.46%); Kerala (93.91%) was the most literate state and Bihar (61.8%) the least.

NOTE

• The Census of India is conducted every 10 years; Census 2011 was the 15th census (7th after Independence), conducted under the Census Act, 1948.

question: Chand Minar at Daulatabad is a 210-feet-high tapering tower divided into _____ storeys.
solution_text:
The correct answer is four.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Chand Minar" at Daulatabad Fort (Maharashtra) is a 210-feet-high tapering tower divided into "four storeys", each marked by a projecting gallery. (चाँद मीनार — चार मंज़िलें)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The Chand Minar was erected in the 15th century (c. 1445) by Ala-ud-din Bahmani (Ahmad Shah Bahmani's successor line) to commemorate the capture of the Daulatabad fort; it shows strong Persian architectural influence.

• It is often called the second most important minar of India after the Qutub Minar of Delhi (which is about 240 feet high and has five storeys).

• Daulatabad (Devagiri) fort is famous as the capital to which Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi (1327).

NOTE

• Famous minars of India: Qutub Minar (Delhi — Qutb-ud-din Aibak/Iltutmish), Chand Minar (Daulatabad), Charminar (Hyderabad — Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, 1591), Fateh Burj (Punjab).

question: Which of the following is a natural indicator for acid and base?
solution_text:
The correct answer is China rose.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "China rose (Hibiscus/Gudhal)" is a natural acid–base indicator. China rose solution turns acidic solutions dark pink (magenta) and basic solutions green. (गुड़हल — प्राकृतिक सूचक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Other natural indicators: litmus (extracted from lichens — red in acid, blue in base), turmeric (yellow in acid/neutral, red in base) and red cabbage juice.

• Synthetic indicators include phenolphthalein (colourless in acid, pink in base) and methyl orange (red in acid, yellow in base).

NOTE

• Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. The pH scale runs 0–14: pH < 7 acidic, pH = 7 neutral, pH > 7 basic. Curry tree, fungi and algae are not used as indicators.

question: Which treatise of Indian classical music was composed by Pandit Sharanga Deva?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sangeet Ratnakar.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Sangeet Ratnakar" (संगीत रत्नाकर) was composed by Pandit Sharanga Deva (Sharngadeva) in the 13th century at the court of the Yadava dynasty of Devagiri (Maharashtra). It is one of the most important Sanskrit treatises on Indian classical music.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Sangeet Ratnakar has seven chapters (hence also called "Saptadhyayi") covering swara, raga, tala, prabandha and dance — it is regarded as authoritative by both Hindustani and Carnatic traditions.

• Sangeet Makarand was written by Narada.

NOTE

• Ancient texts on performing arts: Natya Shastra — Bharat Muni; Brihaddeshi — Matanga (first text to use the word "raga"); Sangeet Ratnakar — Sharngadeva; Sangeet Parijat — Ahobala.

question: The Indian reformer Jyotirao Phule was primarily critical of which social evil of the Indian society?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Caste Discrimination.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Jyotirao (Jyotiba) Phule (1827–1890) was primarily critical of "caste discrimination" and the domination of the lower castes by the upper castes. He worked lifelong for the upliftment of the untouchables, Shudras and women. (जाति भेदभाव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Phule founded the "Satyashodhak Samaj" (Society of Truth Seekers) in 1873 in Maharashtra to fight caste oppression.

• His famous book "Gulamgiri" (Slavery, 1873) attacked the caste system. With his wife Savitribai Phule, he opened one of India's first schools for girls at Pune (1848).

• He was given the title "Mahatma" in 1888.

NOTE

• Social reformers and their focus: Raja Ram Mohan Roy — abolition of Sati (1829); Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar — widow remarriage (1856); Jyotiba Phule / Dr. B. R. Ambedkar — annihilation of caste discrimination.

question: Which of the following states has bicameral (two houses) state legislature?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Karnataka.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Karnataka" has a bicameral state legislature — the Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha) and the Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad). (कर्नाटक — द्विसदनीय विधानमंडल)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Only six states currently have bicameral legislatures: Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Telangana and Uttar Pradesh.

• Under Article 169, Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council if the State Assembly passes a resolution by a special majority.

• The size of a Legislative Council cannot exceed one-third of the Assembly's strength and cannot be less than 40 members (Article 171).

NOTE

• Goa, West Bengal and Punjab have unicameral legislatures (only a Legislative Assembly). Members of Legislative Councils (MLCs) are partly elected by MLAs, local bodies, graduates and teachers, and partly nominated by the Governor.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are INCORRECT?

A) 1833 Charter Act has changed the designation for Governor-General of Bengal, renamed as Governor-General of India.

B) Lord William Bentick was the first Governor General of India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Both A and B (as per the official answer key).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• As per the official SSC answer key, both statements A and B, as worded, were treated as INCORRECT.

• Statement A is inexact because the Charter Act of 1833 did not merely "rename" the post in 1833 — it created the new office of Governor-General of India, with full civil and military control, and the change took effect only in 1834.

• Statement B is likewise treated as inexact — Lord William Bentinck was Governor-General of Bengal from 1828 and assumed the office of Governor-General of India only in 1834, when the Act came into force (also note the misspelling "Bentick" in the statement).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Charter Act of 1833 centralised administration: the Governments of Madras and Bombay lost their legislative powers, a Law Member (Lord Macaulay was the first) was added to the Governor-General's Council, and the East India Company's commercial functions were ended, making it a purely administrative body.

• Standard chronology: Warren Hastings — first Governor-General of Bengal (Regulating Act, 1773); Lord William Bentinck — Governor-General of India from 1834 under the 1833 Act; Lord Canning — first Viceroy of India (Government of India Act, 1858).

NOTE

• Bentinck is remembered for the abolition of Sati (1829), suppression of Thuggee, and making English the medium of higher education (Macaulay's Minute, 1835).

question: What is the term used for the line that a raider must cross to score points in Kabaddi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Baulk line.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In Kabaddi, the "baulk line" is the line in the defenders' half that a raider must cross for the raid to be valid and to be eligible to score points. (बॉक लाइन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The bonus line lies beyond the baulk line — a raider crossing it earns an extra (bonus) point, but only when six or more defenders are on the court.

• The mid line (centre line) divides the court into two halves; the standard Kabaddi court for men measures 13 m × 10 m (women: 12 m × 8 m); each raid is limited to 30 seconds.

• A team has 7 players on court; the raider must chant "kabaddi-kabaddi" in one breath in traditional rules.

NOTE

• Kabaddi facts: the Pro Kabaddi League (PKL) began in 2014; Kabaddi was included in the Asian Games in 1990 (Beijing), where India won the first gold; Kabaddi is the state game of several states, and India has won multiple Kabaddi World Cups.

question:
Identify the personality on the basis of the given clues:

i) She is an acclaimed Bharatanatyam dancer.

ii) She is the recipient of Padma Shri 2016 award.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pratibha Prahlad.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pratibha Prahlad is an acclaimed "Bharatanatyam" dancer who received the "Padma Shri" award in 2016 for her contribution to the arts. (प्रतिभा प्रह्लाद — भरतनाट्यम)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Pratibha Prahlad is also the founder of the Delhi International Arts Festival (DIAF) and of the Prasiddha Foundation.

• Bharatanatyam is the classical dance form of Tamil Nadu, based on Bharat Muni's Natya Shastra; it is traditionally accompanied by Carnatic music.

• Padmaja Reddy is a noted Kuchipudi dancer; Aruna Mohanty is an Odissi dancer.

NOTE

• The eight recognised classical dances of India: Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), Manipuri (Manipur) and Sattriya (Assam).

question: Which of the following folk dances is conducted during the Bwisagu Festival?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bagurumba.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bagurumba" is the folk dance performed during the "Bwisagu Festival", the springtime New Year festival of the Bodo tribe of Assam, celebrated in mid-April. (बागुरुम्बा — बोडो जनजाति)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Bagurumba is also called the "butterfly dance" because of its graceful, fluttering movements; it is performed by Bodo women in colourful dokhona attire.

• Bwisagu corresponds to the Assamese Bohag Bihu (Rongali Bihu) season and involves worship of the deity Bathou, cattle worship, feasting and traditional music.

• Bhortal is a cymbal dance of Assam (Barpeta region); Jhumur is a tea-tribe folk dance of Assam; Bihu dance is performed during the Assamese Bihu festival.

NOTE

• Folk dances of Assam frequently asked in SSC: Bihu, Bagurumba (Bodo), Jhumur, Bhortal, Deodhani. The Bodos are the largest plains tribe of Assam, concentrated in the Bodoland Territorial Region.

question: Cyanobacteria belong to the domain of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Producers.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Cyanobacteria" (blue-green algae) are photosynthetic prokaryotes — they prepare their own food using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide. Hence, in an ecosystem they belong to the category of "producers (autotrophs)". (उत्पादक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Examples of cyanobacteria: Nostoc, Anabaena, Oscillatoria, Spirulina (used as a protein supplement).

• Many cyanobacteria (e.g., Anabaena in the fern Azolla) can fix atmospheric nitrogen, so they are used as biofertilisers in paddy fields.

• Food chain levels: Producers (green plants, algae, cyanobacteria) → Primary consumers (herbivores) → Secondary/Tertiary consumers (carnivores) → Decomposers (bacteria, fungi) break down dead matter.

NOTE

• Cyanobacteria are believed to have created Earth's early oxygen through photosynthesis (the "Great Oxidation Event"). They are prokaryotes (Kingdom Monera), unlike true algae which are eukaryotes.

question: On 10 April 2023, the Government of India launched tourism infrastructure and amenities in the __________________ villages through the 'Vibrant Villages Programme'.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Border.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Vibrant Villages Programme (VVP)" is a centrally sponsored scheme for the comprehensive development of "border villages" along India's northern border. On 10 April 2023, Union Home Minister Amit Shah launched it from Kibithoo village (Arunachal Pradesh). (सीमावर्ती गाँव)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The programme (2022-23 to 2025-26) covers 2,967 villages in 19 districts of Arunachal Pradesh, Sikkim, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh and the UT of Ladakh, with an outlay of about Rs 4,800 crore.

• It provides road connectivity, housing, tourism infrastructure, renewable energy and livelihood opportunities so that border villages are no longer treated as the "last villages" but as the "first villages" of India.

NOTE

• The scheme aims to check migration from border villages, thereby also strengthening national security. It complements the Border Area Development Programme (BADP).

question: In which year did Rohan Bopanna become world number one in the Men's Doubles category of Lawn Tennis?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2024.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Indian tennis star Rohan Bopanna became world No. 1 in Men's Doubles in January 2024, after winning the Australian Open 2024 men's doubles title with his partner Matthew Ebden (Australia). (रोहन बोपन्ना — 2024)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• At 43 years, Bopanna became the oldest player ever to be ranked world No. 1 in doubles and the oldest man to win a Grand Slam doubles title in the Open era.

• He had earlier won the French Open 2017 mixed doubles title (with Gabriela Dabrowski) and the US Open 2023 men's doubles final (runner-up).

• He was honoured with the Padma Shri in 2024 and had earlier received the Arjuna Award.

NOTE

• Indian tennis world No. 1s in doubles: Leander Paes, Mahesh Bhupathi, Sania Mirza (women's doubles) and Rohan Bopanna. The four Grand Slams: Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, US Open.

question: The oceanic trenches or the narrow depressions on the seafloor are formed by reason of:
solution_text:
The correct answer is tectonic activity.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Oceanic trenches" — long, narrow and very deep depressions on the seafloor — are formed by "tectonic activity", specifically at convergent plate boundaries where one plate subducts (sinks) beneath another. (विवर्तनिक गतिविधि — प्रविष्ठन क्षेत्र)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Mariana Trench in the western Pacific is the deepest trench on Earth; its lowest point, the Challenger Deep, is about 11 km (11,034 m) deep.

• Trenches are associated with earthquakes, volcanic arcs and tsunamis — the Pacific "Ring of Fire" is lined with subduction trenches (e.g., Java/Sunda Trench, Peru–Chile Trench, Japan Trench).

• Thermohaline circulation is the density-driven global ocean conveyor; tidal currents are caused by the gravitational pull of the moon and sun — neither creates trenches.

NOTE

• Ocean floor relief features: continental shelf → continental slope → abyssal plain → trench (deepest part). Trenches mark subduction zones where oceanic crust is destroyed, balancing new crust formed at mid-ocean ridges.

question: In the number 0.002609, the number of significant figures is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is four.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In 0.002609, the significant figures are 2, 6, 0 and 9 — i.e., "four" significant figures.

◦ The leading zeros (0.00...) are NOT significant — they only locate the decimal point.

◦ The zero between 6 and 9 IS significant, because zeros between two non-zero digits are always significant.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Rules of significant figures:

◦ All non-zero digits are significant (1234 → 4 sig. figs).

◦ Zeros between non-zero digits are significant (2609 → 4 sig. figs).

◦ Leading zeros are never significant (0.0026 → 2 sig. figs).

◦ Trailing zeros after a decimal point are significant (2.500 → 4 sig. figs).

NOTE

• Significant figures indicate the precision of a measurement. In multiplication/division, the result keeps as many significant figures as the least precise value; in addition/subtraction, it keeps the least number of decimal places.

question: Which of the following is NOT a salient feature of Fundamental Duties of the Indian Constitution?
option_2: There is clear difference between Fundamental Rights and Fundamental Duties.
option_3: Fundamental Duties are both civic and moral in nature.
option_4: They are enforceable by law and can be challenged in court.
solution_text:
The correct answer is They are enforceable by law and can be challenged in court.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Fundamental Duties are "non-justiciable" — they are NOT directly enforceable by the courts, and no one can be punished merely for their violation unless a specific law provides for it. Hence the statement "They are enforceable by law and can be challenged in court" is NOT a salient feature. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — गैर-न्यायोचित)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, as Part IV-A, Article 51A.

• Originally 10 duties; the 11th duty (parents/guardians to provide education to children aged 6–14) was added by the 86th Amendment, 2002.

• They apply only to citizens (not foreigners), and they include both civic duties (respecting the Constitution, National Flag and Anthem) and moral duties (cherishing noble ideals of the freedom struggle).

NOTE

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the USSR (Russia). Fundamental Rights are justiciable; Fundamental Duties and Directive Principles are non-justiciable.

question:
Match the monuments with their respective builders.

Monuments — A. Jama Masjid at Delhi, B. Allahabad Fort, C. Quila I Kunhan Masjid, D. Jama Masjid at Sambhal

Builders — 1. Babur, 2. Sher Shah, 3. Shah Jahan, 4. Akbar
solution_text:
The correct answer is A-3, B-4, C-2, D-1.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• A. Jama Masjid at Delhi — 3. Shah Jahan: built between 1650 and 1656, it is one of the largest mosques in India (originally called Masjid-i-Jahan-Numa).

• B. Allahabad Fort — 4. Akbar: built by Akbar in 1583 at the confluence (Sangam) of the Ganga and Yamuna at Prayagraj.

• C. Quila-i-Kuhna Masjid — 2. Sher Shah: built by Sher Shah Suri (c. 1541) inside the Purana Qila, Delhi.

• D. Jama Masjid at Sambhal — 1. Babur: built in 1526 during Babur's reign (by his general Mir Hindu Beg).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Shah Jahan also built the Taj Mahal, Red Fort (Delhi) and Shahjahanabad; Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri, Agra Fort and Buland Darwaza; Sher Shah Suri built the Grand Trunk Road, Rohtas Fort and his tomb at Sasaram; Babur built mosques at Panipat and Sambhal.

NOTE

• Mughal architecture questions are frequent in SSC — remember dynasty-wise monuments: Babur (1526–30), Humayun, Akbar, Jahangir, Shah Jahan (peak of architecture), Aurangzeb (Bibi ka Maqbara built by his son Azam Shah).

question: According to National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023 (A Progress Review), what is the percentage of the total population who are multidimensionally poor (Headcount Ratio) in Bihar state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 33.76%.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• According to the "National Multidimensional Poverty Index 2023: A Progress Review" released by NITI Aayog, 33.76% of Bihar's population was multidimensionally poor (Headcount Ratio) — the highest among Indian states, though a sharp improvement from 51.89% earlier. (बिहार — 33.76%)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• As per the report, at the national level about 14.96% of India's population was multidimensionally poor (NFHS-5, 2019-21), down from 24.85% (NFHS-4, 2015-16) — about 13.5 crore people escaped multidimensional poverty between 2015-16 and 2019-21.

• The National MPI measures three equally weighted dimensions — Health, Education and Standard of Living — through 12 indicators (nutrition, child & adolescent mortality, maternal health, years of schooling, school attendance, cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets, bank account).

• After Bihar, the poorest states were Jharkhand and Meghalaya; Kerala was among the least poor.

NOTE

• The Global MPI is published by UNDP and OPHI (Oxford). NITI Aayog's National MPI adds two indicators (maternal health and bank account) to the global list of 10.

question: Which of the following rivers flows through Madhya Pradesh?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Betwa.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "Betwa" river rises in the Vindhya Range (Raisen district, Madhya Pradesh), flows north-east through Madhya Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh, and joins the Yamuna at Hamirpur (UP). (बेतवा नदी — मध्य प्रदेश)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Betwa (ancient name Vetravati) flows past Vidisha, Sanchi and Orchha; the Rajghat and Matatila dams stand on it. The Ken–Betwa River Linking Project (India's first river-interlinking project) will connect it with the Ken river in Bundelkhand.

• Shyok — a tributary of the Indus, flows in Ladakh; Sharda (Kali/Mahakali) — flows along the India–Nepal border in Uttarakhand/UP; Bhima — a tributary of the Krishna, flows through Maharashtra, Karnataka and Telangana.

NOTE

• Major rivers of Madhya Pradesh: Narmada, Tapti, Chambal, Betwa, Ken, Son, Shipra. The Yamuna's right-bank tributaries — Chambal, Sindh, Betwa, Ken — all drain the Madhya Pradesh plateau.

question: Who is National Security Advisor of India as of July 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ajit Doval.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Ajit Doval has been the "National Security Advisor (NSA)" of India since May 2014 and continued in office as of July 2023 (reappointed in 2019 and again in 2024 with Cabinet Minister rank). (अजीत डोभाल — राष्ट्रीय सुरक्षा सलाहकार)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Ajit Doval is a former Director of the Intelligence Bureau (IB) and a Kirti Chakra awardee (the first police officer to receive this gallantry award).

• The NSA is the chief advisor to the Prime Minister on national and international security and heads the National Security Council Secretariat; Brajesh Mishra was India's first NSA (1998).

• Rajnath Singh — Defence Minister; Rajiv Gauba — Cabinet Secretary (as of 2023); Sanjeev Sanyal — Member, Economic Advisory Council to the PM.

NOTE

• The National Security Council (NSC), set up in 1998, is the apex body for strategic and security matters, chaired by the Prime Minister.

question: Which port situated at the head of Gulf of Kutch has helped to reduce the pressure at Mumbai port?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kandla.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Kandla Port" (now renamed Deendayal Port) is situated at the head of the Gulf of Kutch in Gujarat. It was developed soon after Independence (after the loss of Karachi port to Pakistan) and has helped reduce the congestion/pressure at Mumbai port. (कांडला — कच्छ की खाड़ी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Kandla is a tidal port and was the site of India's first Export Processing Zone / Free Trade Zone (1965). It handles bulk cargo such as crude oil, salt, foodgrains and fertilisers, serving the rich hinterland of north-western India.

• Haldia is a subsidiary port of Kolkata (a riverine port on the Hugli, West Bengal) built to relieve Kolkata's pressure; Kochi is a natural harbour on the Kerala coast.

• Similarly, Jawaharlal Nehru Port (Nhava Sheva) was built across the harbour to relieve Mumbai port.

NOTE

• India has 13 major ports. Gujarat's other key sites: Mundra (largest private port), Sikka, Okha. Deendayal (Kandla) Port is among India's top ports by cargo volume.

question: What are the three components of the empowerment model in SAPAP of SHGs?
option_1: Social mobilisation, economic development, and education
option_2: Collective empowerment, capital formation, and poverty eradication
option_3: Public resource allocation, capacity building, and microfinance
option_4: Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor
solution_text:
The correct answer is Social mobilisation, capital formation, and capacity building of the poor.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The "South Asia Poverty Alleviation Programme (SAPAP)", supported by the UNDP, followed a three-pronged empowerment model for Self-Help Groups (SHGs): "social mobilisation, capital formation and capacity building of the poor". (सामाजिक गतिशीलता, पूंजी निर्माण और गरीबों का क्षमता निर्माण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• SAPAP was piloted in India in Andhra Pradesh (from 1994-95 in three districts), where women's self-help groups were organised for thrift, credit and livelihoods; its success shaped later programmes such as Velugu/Indira Kranthi Patham and the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM/DAY-NRLM).

• A Self-Help Group (SHG) is a small, informal group (usually 10–20 members, mostly women) that pools savings and provides mutual credit; SHGs are linked to banks under NABARD's SHG–Bank Linkage Programme (1992).

NOTE

• Kudumbashree (Kerala) and SEWA (Gujarat) are other celebrated women's collective models. SHGs are a key instrument of financial inclusion and women's empowerment — a recurring SSC economics topic.

question: Harappa, one of the sites of the Harappan culture, was found in which of the following states of pre-independent India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Punjab.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Harappa", the first-discovered site of the Harappan (Indus Valley) Civilisation, was located in the Montgomery district of Punjab province of pre-independent (undivided) India — now the Sahiwal district of Pakistani Punjab — on the bank of the river Ravi. (हड़प्पा — पंजाब, रावी नदी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• Harappa was excavated in 1921 by Daya Ram Sahni under the direction of Sir John Marshall (then Director-General of the ASI); the civilisation is therefore also called the Harappan Culture.

• Mohenjo-daro (excavated 1922 by R. D. Banerji) lies in Sindh on the Indus; Sutkagendor is in Balochistan; important Indian sites include Lothal and Dholavira (Gujarat), Kalibangan (Rajasthan), Rakhigarhi (Haryana) and Ropar (Punjab).

• Finds at Harappa include granaries, red sandstone male torso, cemetery R-37 and numerous seals.

NOTE

• The Indus Valley Civilisation (c. 2500–1750 BCE, Bronze Age) was known for town planning, grid streets, drainage, standardised weights and the undeciphered pictographic script.
